entities.summary:
Menua, the fifth known king of Urartu, ruled from approximately 810 BC to 786 BC. He played a pivotal role in the political landscape of the ancient Near East, navigating complex alliances and rivalries with neighboring kingdoms.

Menua's reign was marked by significant military campaigns, including the defeat of the Assyrians at the Battle of Halule in 761 BC. This victory secured Urartu's independence and cemented Menua's reputation as a skilled military strategist.

The legacy of Menua extends beyond his own kingdom, influencing the development of the Medes and Persians who would eventually conquer Urartu. His successors would go on to play a crucial role in the Persian Empire's expansion into Greece, a testament to Menua's enduring impact on the ancient world.

"We must not forget the bravery of Menua, who fought against the forces of darkness and secured the freedom of our people." - Urartian Chronicler (c. 700 BC)
